question.leadin: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war.
question.text: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
question.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

swap.text: Merkel belongs to this German political party, which is mainly opposed by the Social Democratic Party.
swap.clue: This party's leaders Ludwig Erhard and Konrad Adenauer sparked an "economic miracle" in its country post-World War II, and it has participated in various "Grand Coalitions" with the Social Democratic Party.

question.text: This prime minister of Prussia worked with Kaiser Wilhelm I to unify Germany. This proponent of "blood and iron" edited the Ems Dispatch as to incite the Franco-Prussian War.
question.clue: This leader stated that the great questions of the day would be decided by "Blood and Iron".

swap.leadin: Name these things associated with the unification of Germany.
swap.text: Germany had been unified after various German lands had come together to defeat France in this war in 1870.
swap.clue: The victors of this war took the territories of Alsace-Lorraine and declared Germany unified just outside of the loser's capital city.

question.leadin: Name these political entities that heavily relied on maritime trade.
question.text: This confederation of German towns and merchants dominated the Baltic Sea trade. After defeating Waldemar IV's forces, this federation received a veto over successors to the Danish throne.
question.clue: It gained power after a treaty giving them access to the Russian port of Novgorod from its base city of Lubeck, but trade there was banned by Ivan III.

swap.leadin: This country's western neighbor tried to prevent other countries from recognizing it by using the Hallstein ("Hahl-shteen") Doctrine.
swap.text: Name this country, whose only president was Wilhelm Pieck ("Vil-helm Peek"). This country's military forces shot the teenager Peter Fechter ("Feck-ter") and let him bleed to death.
swap.answerHtml: East Germany [or the German Democratic Republic; or Deutsche Demokratische Republik; or Ostdeutschland]
swap.clue: This country's secret police, the Stasi, was formed while Walter Ulbricht was in power.

question.leadin: Helmuth von Moltke remarked that although "in its original form [this document] sounded like a parley," now, it was like a "flourish of trumpets in answer to a challenge."
question.text: Name this document edited by Otto von Bismarck, which prompted a neighboring country to declare war on Prussia.
question.clue: This document led to the eventual downfall of the man responsible for the creation of the "Liberal Empire," Emile Ollivier, while the Havas printing of this document notably failed to translate the word "adjutant."

swap.text: This November 9-10th 1938 pogrom was set off by the assassination of Ernst vom Rath. More than 30,000 Jewish men were taken to concentration camps.
swap.answerHtml: Kristallnacht [or Night of Broken Glass or Reichskristallnacht or Pogromnacht or Novemberpogrome]
swap.clue: This event occurred after a failed assassination attempt on Count Johannes von Welczeck ("vell-check"), in which Ernst vom Rath was killed by Herschel Grynszpan.

question.text: 1961 saw a tank standoff at this German border crossing. Peter Fechter's body was stranded here a year later, and it's now home to the Allied Museum.

swap.text: John George I ("the first"), the ruler of this state, was forced to ally with Gustavus Adolphus after his lands were invaded by Tilly shortly before Breitenfeld.
swap.clue: During World War I, George V renamed a royal house named for this region, Coburg, and Gotha to the House of Windsor.

question.leadin: This term may have been first used before the Civil War to refer to Cornelius Vanderbilt.
question.text: What derogatory two-word term was popularized in the Gilded Age to denote predatory business leaders who quashed competition, created monopolies, and paid subsistence wages?
question.clue: Powerful industrialists like Jay Gould and James Fisk in control of the railroad industry became known by this two word term. It reflected their use of exploitative and illegal methods to make money.

swap.text: Among the various construction projects that Ludwig undertook was this castle, which is located close to the Hohenschwangau Castle where Ludwig grew up. Ludwig was inspired by the Singers' Hall of Wartburg Castle when cooking up his plans for this castle.

question.leadin: This entity's youth wing was called the Jugendbund.
question.text: Name this Nazi paramilitary group that was also known as the Brownshirts. Ernst Rohm was one of the founders of this group that was destroyed during the Night of the Long Knives.
question.clue: One member of this group wrote an anthem that began with the words "the Flag on High", and which would be renamed for him after his 1929 assassination.

swap.text: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
swap.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen [or Manfred Albrecht Freiherr von Richthofen; or the Red Baron]
swap.clue: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.

question.text: This Jewish businessman and Weimar-era statesman negotiated the Treaty of Rapallo with the Soviet Union. He was assassinated by the right-wing Operation Consul, after which he was seen as a democratic martyr.
question.clue: The assassins of this German Jewish industrialist and politician may have thought he was an Elder of Zion. This man served as foreign secretary in the Weimar Republic, in which capacity he negotiated the Treaty of Rapallo.

swap.text: Many of the older members of Battalion 101 had been members of these interwar counter-revolutionary paramilitary units. They helped to suppress the Spartacist movement.
swap.clue: This German paramilitary groups largely composed of jobless World War I veterans. They launched the Kapp Putsch in support of Erich Ludendorff.

question.leadin: Sheila Ogilvie's State Corporatism and Proto-Industry argues that this German state's legacy of rent-seeking by worsted-weaving guilds delayed mechanization until after 1870.
question.text: Name this Swabian state where Wilhelm Maybach designed engines at Daimler Motors after the Peace of Pressburg made it and Bavaria into kingdoms. In 1952, it united with the home state of Carl Benz.
question.answerHtml: Württemberg (“WUR-tem-bairk”) [accept Baden-Württemberg or BW or BaWü; accept Kingdom of Württemberg or Königreich Württemberg; accept Duchy of Württemberg or Herzogtum Württemberg; accept Free People’s State of Württemberg or Freier Volksstaat Württemberg; reject “Baden”]

swap.text: This man enacted Ordoliberal policies in West Germany during his tenures as Minister for Economics under Konrad Adenauer and Chancellor, achieving what was called the Wirtschaftswunder, or economic miracle.
swap.clue: A king of this name recognized the end of his rule by giving the Anif Declaration, while another made a countess out of Eliza Gilbert, his mistress better known for performing the Spider Dance as Lola Montez.

question.leadin: This man's forces won a critical victory at the Battle of Tanga, which saw swarms of bees descend on the attackers on the slopes of Kilimanjaro.
question.text: Name this "Lion of Africa," who led a small band of Askaris and German soldiers on a guerilla campaign against hundreds of thousands of Allied troops before finally surrendering, undefeated, at the end of World War I.
question.clue: Another member of this family was the final Republican opponent of extending the PATRIOT Act after filling defeating John Conway and Trey Grayson to fill Jim Bunning's Senate seat.

swap.leadin: Their 1819 passage was sparked by the murder of August von Kotzebue by a student.
swap.text: Name these series of laws that placed government agents in all universities, put all newspapers under government supervision, and expelled overly liberal teachers and students.
swap.clue: Burschenschaften fraternities were banned by these laws, which created an investigatory committee in Mainz to investigate "revolutionary activities" in the German states and gave the Diet censorship powers.
